html:
In the autumn of 1529 the Ottoman sultan Suleiman the Magnificent laid siege to Vienna, the Habsburg capital. It was the first Ottoman attempt on the city, and it failed after about three weeks.

Three years earlier Suleiman had crushed the Hungarian army at Mohács, and Hungary was split between his client king and the Habsburg Ferdinand, brother of Emperor Charles V. Suleiman marched to put his man back on the throne and strike at Ferdinand.

His huge army set out late, slowed by rain, and left its heavy siege guns behind. Vienna's small garrison, under Count Niklas Salm, had blocked the gates and dug countermines against Ottoman tunnels. As winter closed in, with supplies short, the Ottomans made a last assault, then withdrew.

The siege marked the high point of Ottoman reach into central Europe; the frontier settled in Hungary for the next 150 years. A second siege in 1683 ended in a heavy Ottoman defeat, after which the empire began to lose ground in Europe. The threat also helped the Protestant princes in the Holy Roman Empire win concessions from the emperor.
sum: In the autumn of 1529 the Ottoman sultan Suleiman the Magnificent laid siege to Vienna, the Habsburg capital. It was the first Ottoman attempt on the city, and it failed after about three weeks.
